question: Why is active_bytes_read 10.46 GB/token against a 2.58 GB geometry requirement (4.05x)?

measured_reference.note: Live GPU run on sealed Math-Preserve artifact; GPU timestamps present. This worktree did not re-run Metal.

method.what_active_bytes_read_is: Software counter: each matvec/matvec_batch adds the weight tensor's touch size (GPU: Metal buffer lengths for PQ codebooks+codes; native: f32-widened element count × 4). It is NOT a page-fault sampler and NOT host↔device transfer.
method.what_geometry_is: 8 routed experts × 3 projections × 1_378_368 B × 78 layers. Idealised routed-only figure. Ignores dense MLP layers, shared expert, attention, indexer, router, lm_head. Also pretends all 78 layers are sparse (artifact has 3 dense + 75 sparse).
method.static_derivation: Read every relevant tensor's descriptor from General-R0 shard headers (codec, bytes, shape). Multiplied by the forward schedule in gravity_glm::forward_impl (not a guessed site count).
method.live_instrumentation_added: cost_ledger::ActiveByteCategory + record_active_bytes_for(name, bytes) on GPU and CPU matvec paths; per-token active_bytes_by_category in the ledger report.

1_read_granularity.verdict: ELIMINATED as a driver of active_bytes_read
1_read_granularity.evidence: GravityShard::read_tensor copies exactly descriptor.bytes (mmap[start..end]). active_bytes on the GPU path uses Buffer::length() for codebooks+codes, not a shard or page. Kernel page faults are a separate counter (page_faults_minor/major) and do not inflate active_bytes_read.
1_read_granularity.residual_note: mmap may still fault full pages into RSS on first touch; that is not what the 10.46 GB counter measures.

2_dense_lm_head.dense_memo_coverage: SKIPPED for matvec. NativeDenseMemo covers dense()/row() only (norms, biases, embedding rows). lm_head goes through GpuWeightCache as NativeCpu(Vec<f32>) — widened once on first load, then host f32 gemv every token still streams 3.8 GB of the widened matrix.
2_dense_lm_head.memo_budget: DEFAULT_NATIVE_DENSE_MEMO_BUDGET_BYTES = 256 MiB; lm_head alone is 3.8 GB f32 so it cannot reside in the dense memo even if wired.

3_codebooks_re_read_per_expert.evidence: Each gravity-pq payload is self-contained. Expert projections have s=1, card=128, sub=8 → codebooks = 2048 bytes (0.15% of the 1.378 MB payload). Sharing codebooks across experts would save < 0.01 GB/token at 8×3×75.

4_native_rewiden_per_access.verdict: PARTIALLY CONFIRMED — widen tax on natives, not re-widen every access when cached
4_native_rewiden_per_access.dense_path: Norms/biases: memo verifies once + keeps f32; no per-token re-hash after warm.
4_native_rewiden_per_access.matvec_natives: Indexer, router, lm_head: first load widens bf16→f32 into GpuWeightCache; subsequent tokens re-use the f32 vector. active_bytes still bills f32 size every token (correct for host gemv bandwidth).

5_prefetch_readahead.verdict: ELIMINATED as a driver of active_bytes_read
5_prefetch_readahead.evidence: Counter only increments at explicit matvec record sites. OS readahead cannot inflate it.

routed_experts.vs_geometry: Geometry uses ×78 not ×75 (+99 MB geometry over-count on routed alone)

shared_experts.note: Required MoE math; geometry omits entirely

static_byte_ledger_per_token.measured_matvec_calls_note: HAWKING_TG_LEDGER_FINDINGS matvec_calls=538 matches individual (non-batch) sites exactly — schedule fidelity check passed.

accounted_vs_measured.honesty: I can account for 9.34 of the 10.46 GB (89%) from artifact headers × the forward schedule. The remaining ~1.12 GB/token is NOT filled by assumption. Live active_bytes_by_category on device is required to close it.
hypotheses_for_unaccounted_1_12_gb: Metal Buffer::length() returning an allocated size larger than the uploaded payload on some tensors (alignment) — static check at 64 KiB align only recovers ~0.3 GB, not 1.12 GB.

An additional matvec path not in forward_impl (e.g. resident-state dual path if HAWKING_GLM_GPU_RESIDENT_STATE was on during the measured run). Findings show matvec_calls=538 which matches the host-state path, so dual-path is unlikely.
Counter double-count on a subset of tensors in the measured binary revision — category partition on a re-run will prove or kill this.
Variance (min 9.64 / max 11.13) is unexplained by expert-size diversity (all experts are 1_378_368 B). Category breakdown per token will show which class moves.

routed_vs_geometry_delta.kind: geometry uses 78 sparse layers; artifact has 75 — geometry slightly OVER-states routed

true_inflation_inside_static_gb.note: This is real extra traffic vs running at stored bf16. Everything else in the static ledger is weight the forward must touch.

packed_index_decode_and_sha_thread.explanation: GpuWeightCache miss path: raw_payload → read_tensor(verify_hash) + PQ section / native widen. 32 GiB cache budget cannot hold routing-diverse experts across a long generation (~79 GB of expert projections exist). Warm tokens still miss on newly routed experts → re-hash + re-decode. dense() memo only covers small natives (norms), not expert PQ or lm_head matvec loads.
packed_index_decode_and_sha_thread.not_the_same_as_active_bytes: These buckets are CPU time. active_bytes_read still increments on cache hits (weight is re-streamed for the gemv).

ranked_removals.change: Stop billing/running lm_head as host f32. Keep native.bf16 (or pack) on device; gemv in bf16/f16 without widening the full 3.8 GB matrix into a host Vec<f32>.
ranked_removals.wall_time_context: final_head_and_sampling measured 631 ms (26.2%) — largest non-expert bucket
ranked_removals.risk: Medium. Numerics vs host f32 oracle; need parity gate. Does not change the sealed artifact if the runtime consumes native.bf16 as-is.

ranked_removals.change: Reframe geometry for TG gates: full forward touch set (static schedule ~9.34 GB) instead of routed-only 2.58 GB. Removes the fictional 4.05x 'overread' for required non-routed work.
ranked_removals.risk: None to runtime. High value for not chasing ghosts. Keep a separate 'true inflation' metric (widen tax + unaccounted).

ranked_removals.change: Indexer + router: device bf16 gemv (or PQ) without f32 widen.
ranked_removals.risk: Medium. Same numeric class as lm_head. Smaller absolute win.

ranked_removals.change: Close the 1.12 GB unaccounted gap with live active_bytes_by_category (instrumentation landed this change). Do not invent a cause.
ranked_removals.risk: Depends on what the category map shows. Possibly a counter bug (free), possibly more required traffic.

ranked_removals.change: GPU-resident decode state + larger pin-friendly expert working set to cut re-verify/re-decode (83.7 + 63.8 ms). Does not reduce active_bytes_read on hits, but removes repeated first-touch CPU work.
ranked_removals.risk: High coupling with gravity_glm_resident (active lane). Coordinate; do not edit that file from this campaign.
Requires artifact rewrite — FORBIDDEN for sealed Math-Preserve. Skip.

what_not_to_do: Do not change the sealed Math-Preserve artifact.
Do not treat the 4.05x ratio as pure waste — most of the surplus is required non-routed weight traffic geometry never counted.
Do not touch tools/prometheus/, head-to-device lane, or gravity_glm_resident.rs from this campaign.

acceptance: Each token's counters.active_bytes_by_category values sum to counters.active_bytes_read
Compare category means to static_active_byte_schedule in the receipt
